text:
This looks like mid-2008. Fed funds at 3.26% with the 2-year at 2.30% suggests the Fed had been cutting, and a 3-month drop of 1.34pp fits January-March 2008. Headline CPI at 4.12% fits March 2008 (it was 4.0% in March and 3.97% in February). Unemployment at 5.0% matches March 2008 (5.1%) or February (4.8%). Gold up 41% over 12 months fits March 2008, and the 12-month dollar decline of 8.9% fits too. The VIX at 27.6 fits March 2008 as well.

Fed funds averaged about 3.0% in March 2008 and 3.5% in February, so a monthly average of 3.26 might be a blend. The 2-year at 2.30 matches end of March 2008 (about 1.6%) less well, but a monthly average could be about 2.3 in March. The 10-year at 3.78 also fits a March average, which was about 3.5%, or roughly February's 3.74. The 10y-2y spread of 1.48 suggests about March 2008. Core CPI at 2.43 fits as well.

Emerging markets up 21% over 12 months and down 15% over 3 months fits March 2008. Payrolls averaging +97k over 3 months is a poor fit, though; in early 2008 the figure was negative. The 3-month change of +20 and a 12-month change of -80 are inconsistent with that, unless later revisions are in play. Given the unemployment rate at 5.0, I'll go with March 2008.
